question.text: Strong reducing behaviour of $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{PO}_{2}$ is due to

options.text: presence of one $-\mathrm{OH}$ group and two $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bonds
high electron gain enthalpy of phosphorus
presence of two -OH groups and one $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bond

solution.text: The acids which contain $\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{H}$ bond have strong reducing properties. Thus $\mathrm{H}_{3} \mathrm{PO}_{2}$ acid is good reducing agent as it contains two P-H bonds. For example, it reduces $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$ to metallic silver.
